reasoning: This was a single-arm rollover study of tremelimumab in 37 patients with various solid tumors. Working through the causal chain: 1) TARGET ENGAGEMENT: No PD/PK data or biomarker evidence provided to confirm CTLA-4 engagement, though the dose (15 mg/kg) is in the expected therapeutic range. 2) PATHWAY MODULATION: No evidence of immune activation or T-cell biomarker changes reported. 3) CLINICAL TRANSLATION: The median disease-free survival of 3.0 days is extremely poor, suggesting minimal to no clinical benefit. 4) POPULATION EFFECTS: No subgroup analyses reported. 5) CONFOUNDERS: This appears to be a rollover/compassionate use study for patients who had previously received tremelimumab, suggesting they may have been treatment-refractory. The extremely short disease-free survival and lack of any efficacy signal, combined with notable safety issues (hypersensitivity reactions in 16% of patients), indicates failure at multiple levels of the causal chain.

failure_modes.evidence: While target engagement cannot be confirmed from available data, the extremely short median disease-free survival of 3.0 days suggests that even if CTLA-4 was engaged and immune biology was modulated, it did not translate to meaningful clinical benefit

This was a rollover study for patients who had previously received tremelimumab in other protocols, suggesting a heavily pre-treated, potentially treatment-refractory population that may not be optimal for demonstrating efficacy
